D.treatment: UDL Math and Design Thinking professional development with empathy interviews

O.outcome_detail: understanding UDL as a dynamic, moment-to-moment design process

cells.quote: Across data sources, the educators in our study attributed shifts in their beliefs and practices to empathy, both as a value and a practice of empathy interviews. Educators described UDL as moment-to-moment decision making during instruction based on empathic relationships with students.
cells.note: The study reports shifts across pre/post surveys and focus groups, but the supplied text does not specify the professional-development duration or a formal comparison design.

D.treatment: UDL Math and Design Thinking professional development centered on empathy
D.comparison: educators’ prior deficit-oriented understandings of disability

O.outcome_detail: beliefs about disability and disabled students’ mathematical capacity

cells.quote: Educators reported shifts away from deficit thinking about disability, towards instruction from the perspective of their disabled students.
cells.note: The reported shift was documented for a majority but not all participants, according to the wiki entry; the supplied study text does not provide a numerical effect estimate.

O.outcome_detail: Change in Dementia Knowledge Assessment Scale score

cells.quote: Participants with the least exposure to dementia obtained the greatest increases in dementia knowledge scores (after adjusting for general education) after taking the UDMOOC. This UDMOOC × exposure interaction was signi ﬁcant ( F(7,4886) = 87.8, p < 0.001), and suggests an equalising capacity for the UDMOOC to increase dementia knowledge across exposure cohorts (see Fig. 1 for further illustration).
cells.note: The comparison concerns differential pre-post improvement across prior-exposure groups.

cells.quote: However, knowledge of all participant groups showed substantial improvements after completion of the UDMOOC. This was shown regardless of educational background and previous experience of dementia, and group differences after completing the UDMOOC were minimised.
cells.note: Educational attainment was associated with baseline knowledge, while post-course improvements occurred across all education groups and reduced group differences.

At post-test, 2567 (52%) of participants achieved the target score, compared with 555 (11%) participants at pre-test, clearly demonstrating the potential of this mode of online learning to increase levels of dementia knowledge across broad sections of the community to levels observed in the most knowledgeable segment.

D.treatment: participants with the least dementia exposure

O.outcome_detail: change in DKAS knowledge score after the UDMOOC

cells.quote: Participants with the least exposure to dementia obtained the greatest increases in dementia knowledge scores (after adjusting for general education) after taking the UDMOOC. This UDMOOC × exposure interaction was signiﬁcant ( F(7,4886) = 87.8, p < 0.001), and suggests an equalising capacity for the UDMOOC to increase dementia knowledge across exposure cohorts.
Both before and after the UDMOOC, higher levels of educa-tional attainment and higher levels of exposure to dementia were associated with higher probability of achieving the target score.
cells.note: The study reports an association rather than a printed effect size for this education-group contrast.
